items.title: Rio de Janeiro's "homegrown" LLM appears to be a merge of an existing model
items.author: unrvl22
items.summary: Rio de Janeiro's "homegrown" LLM is a blend of Nex-N2 Pro and Qwen3.5-397B. It was presented as a fine-tuned Qwen3.5 model but is actually 60% Nex-N2 Pro and 40% Qwen3.5-397B. This model was released by IplanRIO.

items.title: Chaosnet (1981)
items.author: RGBCube
items.summary: Chaosnet was an early local area network protocol developed in 1981 to connect Lisp machines at MIT. It used a contention-based approach with a pseudo-slotted feature to reduce collisions. The network operated over a range of up to 1000 meters.

items.title: A short history of Cerro Torre, the most controversial mountain (2012)
items.author: joebig
items.summary: Cerro Torre, a mountain in Patagonia, is known for its controversial first ascent by Cesare Maestri in 1959. Recent debates involve American climbers Hayden Kennedy and Jason Kruk. The mountain's history remains contentious due to disputed claims.

items.title: AI is code – and can't be prompted into being smarter
items.author: wglb
items.summary: AI systems are fundamentally code and cannot be made smarter through prompting alone; they can be manipulated by input, posing risks like supply chain attacks and poor code quality. This is a significant concern as humans can subvert AI operations.

items.title: Perlisisms (1982)
items.author: tosh
items.summary: Alan Perlis' "Perlisisms" from 1982 are concise programming epigrams highlighting the complexities and philosophies of software development. Key points include the importance of understanding programs deeply and the inevitability of differences in code interpretations.

items.title: The hallucinogenic mushroom that contains no known psychedelic
items.author: thunderbong
items.summary: Lanmaoa asiatica is a hallucinogenic mushroom that lacks known psychoactive compounds like psilocybin or muscimol, suggesting an undiscovered hallucinogenic compound. Reports indicate it causes vivid hallucinations, particularly of little people, despite lacking recognized biosynthetic genes.

items.title: Chopped, Stored, Secured – The Story of the Hash Function
items.author: denismenace
items.summary: A hash function maps data to a fixed-size value, ensuring data integrity and quick retrieval. It produces a unique hash code for each input, which is crucial for secure data storage. Hash functions are used in cryptography to verify data without revealing the original content.

items.title: I indexed 669 GB of my GoPro videos using my M1 Max computer and local ML models
items.author: iliashad
items.text:
TLDR: I had 2,207 GoPro videos, and I need to rewatch them to find interesting moments from my cycling journey. I built a project to index them locally on my M1 Max using open-source ML models, search for those moments, and send the best clips straight to my DaVinci Resolve timeline. I indexed 628 videos (668.68 GB, 15h 13m 18s of footage duration), more details in the metrics table in the last section of this article.

Full article: https://iliashaddad.com/blog/i-indexed-6
items.summary: The indexing of 669 GB of GoPro videos was accomplished using an M1 Max computer and local machine learning models. The project involved 2,207 videos and utilized an agent for finding and editing moments. The results were sent directly to DaVinci Resolve for further editing.

items.title: How to earn a billion dollars
items.author: kingstoned
items.summary: To earn a billion dollars, start a successful company or invest in long-term, high-growth stocks. Few become billionaires through salaried work alone. Patience and strategic investments are key.

items.title: Linux 7.1
items.author: berlianta
items.summary: Linux 7.1 introduces a new in-kernel NTFS driver and drops support for Intel's 486 processors. It also includes AMD Zen 6 CPU support.

items.title: Not everyone is using AI for everything
items.author: yegg
items.summary: Not everyone uses AI for everything; many people avoid or limit its use due to personal preferences or concerns. AI is often used in specific contexts, especially in professional settings where it's mandated. Some individuals prefer traditional methods over AI.

items.title: Quivers: A year of linear algebra by drawing arrows
items.author: ibobev
items.summary: Quivers are directed graphs used in linear algebra to represent vector spaces and linear maps. They generalize linear representations, often visualized by drawing arrows. Quiver representations assign vector spaces to vertices and linear maps to arrows.

items.title: Inverse Rubric Optimization: A testbed for agent science
items.author: etherio
items.summary: Inverse Rubric Optimization (IRO) is a research method for studying long-horizon tasks in agent science. It addresses the challenges of noise in complex, extended tasks. IRO is highlighted in recent studies by Fulcrum Inc.

items.title: Ponytail – make your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room
items.author: mellosouls
items.summary: Ponytail is a tool that makes your AI agent think like a lazy senior developer, minimizing code and eliminating unnecessary boilerplate. It asks if something needs to exist before writing code and scales the effort to write the minimum required code.

items.title: US and Iran reach cease fire agreement
items.author: koolba
items.summary: The US and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire and initiate new nuclear talks. The deal is pending approval from US President Trump. This marks a significant step towards easing tensions between the two nations.

items.title: Bacteria can learn and form memories without a brain (Carnegie Mellon)
items.author: indynz
items.summary: Bacteria can learn from past experiences, store memories across generations, and adapt to changing environments without a brain or nervous system, as shown by researchers at Carnegie Mellon University. This ability is due to their ability to encode memories of past environments to guide future behavior.

items.title: Did Anthropic ask for this?
items.author: ad8e
items.summary: Anthropic has asked users for feedback on how they seek personal guidance from its AI, Claude. This reflects their focus on user interaction and adherence to ethical guidelines. Anthropic uses this data to improve its AI's helpfulness.
